title: Derivative ideal versus cumulative Taylor-rank minors
statement:
Let $L$ be a field of characteristic zero, $A=L[[W,Z]]$, and $K\subset A$ be an ideal [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Fix a finitely generated orthant diagram $D=\bigcup_i(\alpha_i+\mathbf N^n)$ with distinct minimal vertices ordered by nondecreasing total degree, zero $W$ components and essential variables $Z$. Put $d_i=|\alpha_i|$ and form the first-vertex quotient supports $\Delta_i$. Group vertices by equal degree; let $s_\ell$ be the last index of block $\ell$ and $Z^\ell$ its accumulated essential variables. Assume $f_i\in K$ have order $d_i$, unique homogeneous division by their initial forms for every degree prefix with these supports, and $K=\{\sum_iq_if_i:\operatorname{supp}q_i\subset\Delta_i\}$. Assume also that for each accumulated block one can choose $\alpha_{i(j)}=\beta_j+e_j$, $i(j)\le s_\ell$, with $g_j=\partial_Z^{\beta_j}f_{i(j)}\in(Z^\ell)$ and invertible $Z^\ell$-Jacobian at zero, and that $\partial_{Z^\ell}^{\beta}f_i\in(Z^\ell)$ for $i>s_\ell$, $\beta$ in that block's restricted orthant diagram and $|\beta|\le Q$, where $Q\ge\max_i d_i-1$ [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. For $t\ge0$, form the finite matrix $B_t$ with columns $Y^\eta f_i(X+Y)\bmod(Y)^{t+1}$, $|\eta|\le t$, in the monomial basis of $A[Y]/(Y)^{t+1}$; $X=(W,Z)$. Write $r_t=\operatorname{rank}_L B_t(0)$ and let $J_t$ be the ideal generated by the $(r_t+1)$-minors of $B_t$. For every $q\ge\max_i d_i-1$,
$$\sum_{t=0}^qJ_t=(\partial^\nu f_i:|\nu|<d_i).$$
Use the convention $\max\varnothing=0$ for an empty vertex list, and interpret $d_i-1$ bounds over the integers. The minors ideals [def-trf-minor-ideal] are independent of the finite generators of $K$. In a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] chart their construction commutes with Taylor expansion from any regular generators of the defining ideal. The zero set of $\sum_{t=0}^qJ_t$ is, as a germ at the distinguished point, the Hilbert--Samuel equality locus once $q$ is sufficiently large and the Taylor-module dimension functions take finitely many local values. Hilbert--Samuel here means $t\mapsto\dim_L A/(K+(X)^{t+1})$, including the extended Taylor-module interpretation at nonclosed scheme points. In the finite-type assertion the chart is smooth over a characteristic-zero field, $L$ is the residue field of the distinguished point, and $K$ is the Taylor extension of the ideal defining the closed subscheme.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-supported-taylor-presentation-pivots] with $a_i=(0,\alpha_i)$. Since every supported coefficient lies in $A$, supported generation implies $K=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$. This and homogeneous division give $B'_t$ with the same image as $B_t$, the rank formula, unit pivots $C_t$, and generator independence of $J_t$. This also covers a zero-dimensional fibre quotient without using a negative Fitting index.

source.place: BM Definitions 7.9--7.13 and Theorem 7.14, supported presentation and pivot; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 supplies the route.

proof.text:
Put $E=(\partial^
u f_i:|
u|<d_i)$ and $S_t=\sum_{u\le t}J_u$. Step 1 supplies the equal column spans, rank count and unit pivot required by [lem-trf-taylor-minor-derivative-bounds]; its good columns correspond bijectively to $\gamma\in D$, $|\gamma|\le t$, by $(i, eta)\mapsto a_i+ eta$, since first-vertex supports partition $D$. Thus $J_t\subseteq E$ for every $t$. Its cofactor relation gives $\partial^\gamma f_i\in J_t+(\partial^\alpha f_i:\alpha\in D,|\alpha|\le t)$ for $t<d_i$, $\gamma
otin D$, $|\gamma|\le t$. Since $J_t\subseteq S_t$ and $S_{t+1}=S_t+J_{t+1}$, the family $I_t=S_t$ is increasing and satisfies the required relation.

source.place: BM Lemma 7.15 and Theorem 7.14, reverse inclusion; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 supplies the route.

proof.text: Assume the vertex list is nonempty and all its degrees are positive. Apply [lem-trf-block-low-derivative-recovery] to $I_t=S_t$ and the given block derivatives. Its Jacobian and later-block hypotheses are exactly those of the item; the derivative bound needed is $\max_i(d_i-1)\le Q$. The last block gives $E\subseteq S_{\max_i d_i-1}\subseteq S_q$. Step 2 gives $S_q\subseteq E$, proving equality, even for $q>Q$.

source.place: BM Remark 7.16, Lemma 7.17 and Theorem 7.14, block induction; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 supplies the route.

proof.text: If the list is empty, supported generation gives $K=0$ and $B_t$ has no columns, so $J_t=E=0$. If a vertex has degree zero, minimality leaves only $0$; its generator has nonzero constant coefficient and hence is a unit. Writing its translated series as $c+u$ with $c\in L^\times$ and $u\in(X,Y)$, the inverse is $c^{-1}\sum_{v\ge0}(-u/c)^v$, reduced modulo $(Y)^{t+1}$. Thus multiplication is invertible in $T_t$, all ranks are full, $J_t=0$, and $E=0$ since there are no derivatives of negative order. This includes no transverse variables and empty matrices.

source.place: BM Definitions 7.9--7.13, empty and unit cases; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 supplies the route.

proof.text: In a smooth finite-type etale coordinate chart, apply [lem-trf-regular-taylor-minor-equality-germ] to the regular generators and the distinguished point. It gives Taylor compatibility and generator independence of the regular minors, and identifies their common vanishing germ, for all sufficiently large $q$, with equality of the full extended Taylor-dimension functions. These are the Hilbert--Samuel functions in the statement, retaining all relative variables at nonclosed points. Choose $q$ at least both its finite-separation cutoff $q_0$ and $\max_i(d_i-1)$, with the stated empty-list convention. The formal equality of steps 3--4 then applies at the same cutoff, giving all remaining clauses.

source.place: BM Remarks 9.1 and 9.5(2), Taylor compatibility and equality germ; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 supplies the route.

theorem formalStratumIdeal_eq_lowDerivativeIdeal
    {L : Type u} [Field L] [CharZero L] {m n s : ℕ}
    (α : Fin s → Fin n →₀ ℕ) (K : Ideal (MvPowerSeries (Fin m ⊕ Fin n) L))
    (f : Fin s → MvPowerSeries (Fin m ⊕ Fin n) L) (Q : ℕ)
    (hdegree : ∀ i j : Fin s, i < j → (α i).degree ≤ (α j).degree)
    (hminimal : ∀ i j : Fin s, α i ≤ α j → i = j)
    (hessential : ∀ j : Fin n, ∃ i : Fin s, 0 < α i j)
    (horder : ∀ i : Fin s, f i ∈ K ∧ (f i).order = ((α i).degree : ℕ∞))
    (hdivision : homogeneousDivision α f)
    (hgeneration : ∀ h ∈ K, ∃ a : Fin s → MvPowerSeries (Fin m ⊕ Fin n) L,
      h = ∑ i : Fin s, a i * f i ∧
        ∀ i : Fin s, supported (a i) (inDelta (fun j ↦ fullVertex m (α j)) i))
    (hblocks : ∀ b : ℕ, (∃ i : Fin s, (α i).degree = b) →
      ∃ (pick : {j : Fin n // essential α b j} → Fin s)
        (β : {j : Fin n // essential α b j} → Fin n →₀ ℕ),
        (∀ j, α (pick j) = β j + Finsupp.single j.val 1 ∧
          (α (pick j)).degree ≤ b ∧
          iteratedPartial (fullVertex m (β j)) (f (pick j)) ∈ transverseIdeal α b) ∧
        IsUnit (Matrix.det (fun j l : {j : Fin n // essential α b j} ↦
          MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff (MvPowerSeries.pderiv L (Sum.inr l.val)
            (iteratedPartial (fullVertex m (β j)) (f (pick j)))))))
    (hlater : ∀ b : ℕ, (∃ i : Fin s, (α i).degree = b) →
      ∀ i : Fin s, b < (α i).degree → ∀ δ : Fin n →₀ ℕ,
        δ.degree ≤ Q → (∀ j : Fin n, δ j ≠ 0 → essential α b j) →
        inDiagram α b δ →
        iteratedPartial (fullVertex m δ) (f i) ∈ transverseIdeal α b)
    (hQ : ∀ i : Fin s, ((α i).degree : ℤ) - 1 ≤ (Q : ℤ))
    (q : ℕ) (hq : ∀ i : Fin s, ((α i).degree : ℤ) - 1 ≤ (q : ℤ)) :
    formalStratumIdeal f q = lowDerivativeIdeal α f
